name: pges-manual-evaluation
description: One 54-case manual evaluation set. The same cases are checked against two query formulas: permissive base PGES and the exact strict PGES formula. The strict formula adds a 10 s no-event prefix, S without P throughout the seizure, T without C and C without T in their windows, and P without S after the offset. All exclusions are part of the formula; adjacent event boundaries are treated as meets.

formula.name: PGES
formula.notes: x = seizure anchor, a = tonic window length, b = clonic window length, c = EEG suppression length. P must cover [x+a+b, x+a+b+c); the permissive base query may use a P interval that begins earlier.

evaluation_instructions.goal: Check whether the query result accurately expresses the meaning of the PGES formula.
what_to_verify: Base PGES: for valid cases, is there at least one witness with correct x,a,b,c?
Base PGES: do the used intervals match the expected relation (e.g. P covers the seizure offset and extends for c seconds, even if the P interval began earlier)?
Strict PGES: every strict match should also be a base match, and all five strict conjuncts must hold at one witness.
Strict PGES: for each rejection, identify which conjunction fails: the 10 s no-event prefix, S∧¬P, T∧¬C, C∧¬T, or P∧¬S.
Strict PGES: overlap is allowed when T∧¬C and C∧¬T each have a point; postictal T/C is allowed because only S is excluded; c may end before the full P interval.
Are wrong temporal relations and labeling errors correctly rejected by the intended query?
Does multi-episode counting match patterns vs patients?
Does changing the c >= n filter behave correctly?
Does the support trace show all five strict conjuncts satisfied for a match?
evaluation_instructions.notes: There is one evaluation set, not separate base/strict datasets. Both query formulas are applied to every case. The page reports expected agreement at c >= 0; both base and strict should read 54/54. Then inspect individual witnesses and conjunct failures.

base.name: PGES base
base.semantics: Permissive reference query. T and C only need to occur in their windows, so their intervals may overlap or extend outside S, and P may begin before the seizure offset.

strict.name: PGES strict
strict.semantics: All conditions are inside the formula. ∅ means no S/T/C/P event. Strict evaluation treats event intervals as half-open, so adjacent boundaries meet rather than overlap. c is any positive run of P∧¬S; the playground uses the maximal run and then applies the c filter. T and C may overlap as long as T∧¬C and C∧¬T each have a witness, and postictal T/C is allowed because the final conjunct excludes S, not all events.
